In

on the plane,
one of them was Li Tz'u-wen, the member of the Executive

were Chou Hua-

When the plane landed the waist belt for Mr. Li got
loose and thereby his left arm and ankle were broken.
Mr. Chou was
slightly wounded by rubbing against something and Mrs. Chou was
rubbed off a piece of skin from her right head.
The
rest were all
safe.
Through the introduction of Mr. Yang General Chou gave the
following information to the correspondent:
On March 5, 2 p.m. he received an order from General Chiang
Kai-shek transferring him to the field headquarters at Hankowand
Mr. Li was instructed by the Central Government to proceed to Nanking
before the 7th to hold a meeting there. Consequently both of them rode
in the same plane.
The weather was already unfavorable when the plane left Kweiyang
for Chungking.
With a view to maintaining its regular service and
credit,
however, it took off heading for Chungking.
Arriving at
Tungtze the plane wound round the mountains.
Usually when it reaches
and finds its way out of the mountain ranges the Yangtze River c
But this time the ranges were wrapped in a cloak of
dense fog and it was terribly cold.
People could not see one another.
supremely dangerous to fly in such a trying circumstances.
By a bit of carelessness everything would become perished.
that time the pilots took much care and concentrated their mind to
cope with the situation.
Among the mountain ranges enveloped in
heavy fog the plane had for several times escaped from bumping against
the sharp cliffs.
It was to the imperturbable management of the pilots
that nothing had happened.
As the fog was so dense that there was no evidence to safeguard
the future security
the pilots decided to veer its direction and
climb up as high as 22,000 feet to keep out the fog.
At the same
as the weather around Kweiyang was also unfavorable the plane
was turned toward Yunnanfu.
Unfortunately there were also heavy
clouds on the way.
Nothing could be seen except a vast expanse of
The pilots and passengers while just
free from danger were
again thrown into hazardous position.
Everybody closed his eyes and
waited to die. It was shown on the gasoline meter that there was
only a supply of 40 gallons left. . Not & single piece of land could
be seen from the plane.
During that time the plane could not return
to Kweiyang and it was unknown where they should go forward.
it was feared that the plane might collide with mountains
Under such circumstances drops of perspiration flowed down
from the forehead
of the pilot.
With a view to making a narrow
the pilot decided
through the clouds as he thought in case
it happened to land on a plain everybody could saved from death.
Thereupon he bagan to descend.
When the plane went through the
clouds it was found that there were precipitious cliffs down.
this time the passengers realized that they could not live any longer,

all waiting for death.i The pilot managed to struggle to the last
moment.
In a little while the plane landed in a dry stream which
separated two precipitious cliffs of almost 10,000 feet high each.

There was fire at the head of the plane. One
person was thrown out of several feets from the broken tail.
The
rest passengers were also shaken out from the plane.
The pilot
hastened to put off the fire with the engine behind him.
When the passengers were saved by the pilot it was found that
the place was nothing but mountain ranges.
Strong wind was blowing
and ice was freezing.
It was 6:30 p.m.
One of the passengers, General
Chou, and the pilots went forward to find if there were any families
Mr. Li, who was heavily hurted, remained beside the
with the radioman.
Before long
they found a village consist-
ing of four or five families.
Immediately they took up lodging in
a family named Yuan and at the same time they learned that the
place was called San Tan Ho or Chin Chu Ping.
They also hired some
country coolies to carry
the wounded persons
to the village.
following day they all proceeded to Itzukung.
On the 6th Mr. Black made a flight to Kutsing with Fleet to

weather he came back.
on the 7th the China National Aviation Corporation sent a

On the 10th the Douglas arrived at Yunnanfu and left the
following day.
On the 11th the Provinclal Kuomintang at Yunnanfu sent three
members of its staff in a motor car to Pingi to carry Mr. li to

He arrived on the 13th here and is receiving medical
Calmett Hospital.
It is learned that he will not be
recovered until two months later.
